subject: Pilot readiness: load profile & runbook acceptance
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam@zenpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot readiness: load profile & runbook acceptance

Hi Liam / ZenPay team —

Thanks again for a productive demo and walk-through today. As promised, here’s a concise recap of the technical and commercial items we discussed and the proposed next steps to kick off a 4‑week trial (POC) with Redwood: 

Summary of agreed trial goals (candidate success criteria)
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency under 350ms for typical NLU requests (avg tokens ~40).
- Throughput: sustain steady state of 120 RPS for the canonical endpoint with spikes to 800 RPS for up to 30s.
- Error rate: <0.5% client-visible errors during trial.
- Cost visibility: token-level cost report for each route; target gross token spend cap $5,000 for the 4 weeks.
- Quality: no more than 8% regression on our red team prompt set compared to baseline (you’ll provide the eval prompts).

Workload profile we captured on-call (please confirm or correct):
- Endpoint: /text/generate (primary), /chat/completions (secondary).
- Steady RPS: 120 (mostly single-turn queries).
- Concurrency: typical concurrency 30 connections; concurrency bursts up to 220.
- Token lengths: input tokens median 18, 90th pct 60; output tokens median 35, 90th pct 120.
- Burst pattern: daily peak around 09:00–10:30 PT; occasional campaign-driven bursts (estimated 600–800 RPS for 20–45s).

Attachments I’m including in this thread: the workload CSV you dropped in the call, our mutual action plan draft, and Redwood runbook template (stubs).

Next concrete steps (owners & dates):
1) ZenPay: confirm the workload CSV + attach the eval prompt set by EOD Mon 2027-05-24 — owner: Liam.
2) Redwood (Aditya): validate the CSV, map to a trial config (batching, KV cache policy, quantization suggestion) by Wed 2027-05-26.
3) Redwood (Marcus): estimate capacity reservation and propose an autoscaling/burst policy by Fri 2027-05-28.
4) Mutual: sign-off on trial MOP and schedule test ramp (start window target Mon 2027-06-07).

A few open technical clarifications from our side (Aditya / Marcus highlighted these on-call):
- Will ZenPay allow prefix caching for repeated system prompts? (affects KV cache hit rates)
- Expected distribution of API keys per session/user agent (single shared key vs many per-user keys).
- Any IP egress controls or VPC requirements we should pre-configure for Private mode?

If you’re good with the goals above, I’ll send the MOP + runbook for signature and flag internal capacity for the trial window.

Best,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: zenpay_poc_workload.csv (csv), zenpay_mutual_action_plan.docx (docx), redwood-runbook-template.md (markdown)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Liam Carter <liam@zenpay.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot readiness: load profile & runbook acceptance

Grace — quick follow-up from our systems team after reviewing the CSV you attached:

Thanks for the thorough summary. A couple of engineering clarifications we need from ZenPay before we finalize the trial config: 
- Tokenization baseline: can you confirm the tokenizer you use for pre/post processing (it impacts per-token billing and batch packing)?
- Request size distribution: the CSV shows many outliers ~3–4k tokens; are those long-form batch jobs or occasional export flows? We should mark those as backfill if they aren’t in-scope for the POC.
- Auth: will you use a single API key for Redwood or per-environment keys? Per-key metrics enable better per-tenant throttling.

Preliminary Redwood config suggestions (we’ll refine once ZenPay confirms):
- Sequence length cap 4096; prefer int8 quantized model variant for the trial to control cost.
- Continuous batching target: 16–32 tokens per batch for /text/generate route.
- KV cache: recommend enabling prefix caching for repeated system messages; we can quantify expected cache hit rate once we see the prompt set.

If we can get the tokenizer and the eval prompts from Liam by Monday, I’ll produce a concrete capacity proposal and expected token spend estimate.

- Aditya
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

On Sat, May 22, 2027 at 3:02 PM Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Liam / ZenPay team —
> 
> Thanks again for a productive demo and walk-through today. As promised, here’s a concise recap...
From: Liam Carter <liam@zenpay.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: ZenPay Ops <ops@zenpay.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot readiness: load profile & runbook acceptance

Thanks Grace — summary looks correct from our side and appreciate the clarity. A few items/answers below: 

Confirmed items:
- We will provide the eval prompt set (customer red-team prompts) and the full tokenized CSV by Mon EOD (2027-05-24).
- Our primary endpoint is the single-turn NLU service (single prompt -> single completion) — the long outliers are a nightly reconciliation job and can be excluded from the POC.
- We'll provide per-environment API keys (staging/test/production) for the trial.

Answers to technical Qs:
- Tokenizer: we use an in-house wrapper around tiktoken (gpt2) — I’ll export tokenized counts in the CSV.
- Prefix caching: yes we can allow repeated system prompts; happy to mark the most common templates for cache-friendly routing.
- Networking: no special VPC at trial start; public endpoints are fine for the first week — we’ll revisit VPC or peering for production.

Success criteria tweak: upweight latency requirement to 90th percentile <300ms (we've got a tighter UX requirement for the main flow). If Redwood can demonstrate that during the trial window for the canonical payload, we'll mark latency as met.

Action items from ZenPay (owner = Liam):
- Upload tokenized CSV + eval prompt set by Mon EOD (2027-05-24).
- Confirm a single trial escalations contact (Ops | ops@zenpay.com).

Happy to proceed on the timeline you suggested. Let me know if you want a short sync with your infra team before we start the ramp.

—Liam
Liam Carter
VP Platform Engineering | ZenPay

Subject: Re: Pilot readiness: load profile & runbook acceptance

Great — thanks for the confirmations and the tightened latency target, Liam. Quick acknowledgment and updated plan: 

Updated trial acceptance criteria (per your note)
- Latency: 90th percentile < 300ms for canonical NLU flow (median output ~35 tokens).
- Steady-state: 120 RPS with burst handling to 800 RPS (30–45s bursts).
- Error rate < 0.5% and quality regression <= 8% on your eval prompts.

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
- Liam (ZenPay): drop tokenized CSV + eval prompts to the Drive link and confirm trial escalation contact by EOD Mon 2027-05-24.
- Aditya: produce the trial capacity proposal + expected token spend by Wed 2027-05-26.
- Marcus: provide autoscale/burst policy recommendation and prelim capacity reservation by Fri 2027-05-28.
- Grace: send MOP + runbook for signature once we have the CSV and prompts.

I’ll schedule a 30‑minute infra handoff for Thu 2027-05-27 at 09:00 PT to walk through the runbook and ramp plan — invite to follow.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Grace
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
